archive_08_001.speaker: narrator
archive_08_001.text: Yue spent her fifty-sixth day off at the small mountain market. The ridge road remained restricted, but local households could reach the village square by cleared footpaths. A pot seller had arranged his wares under a patched awning, and a shoemaker warmed his needle between his fingers. Yue bought a spool of blue thread and an apple bruised on one side. She carried no archive case. Her ordinary sword stayed covered at her hip while she considered whether the bruise justified the price.

archive_08_002.speaker: narrator
archive_08_002.text: A paper stall stood near the well, offering route tables, household calendars and copies of common-right extracts. A woman buying a grazing sheet asked the seller whether its round red mark meant she could take it straight to the district office. He said it was a clean copy of the archive's text. The answer did not meet the question. Yue looked at the mark from the public side of the stall. It resembled a simplified archive seal but belonged to the seller's own shop stamp, whose small outer words were difficult to read.

archive_08_003.speaker: narrator
archive_08_003.text: She asked him what the sheet promised. He pointed to the grazing fields and said people paid less here than they paid for a certified extract uphill. The woman repeated her question about the district office. This time he admitted he did not know what office would accept it. Yue explained that a shop-marked reference copy and an archive-certified comparison were different things. The seller bristled at the sword before listening to the words. She moved her hand away from its covered hilt and gave him the same explanation at an ordinary speaking distance.

archive_08_004.speaker: narrator
archive_08_004.text: The woman decided not to buy yet and asked where she could check the requirement. Yue pointed her toward the public district notice at the receiving house and the office named for grazing applications. She did not declare the stall's wording false without comparing its source. The seller accused her of frightening away a customer. She said the customer had asked a question he had not answered. It was her rest day, and she had no enforcement appointment. She left after noting the publicly offered sheet title and source number, buying no secret sample.

archive_08_005.speaker: narrator
archive_08_005.text: He found her at the apple stall and knew immediately why she looked annoyed. The paper seller had copied one of He's route tables before, including an old bridge opening hour that was no longer reliable. He had corrected it after a driver complained. He said the man was impatient, hungry for sales and usually willing to fix an error once it cost him a customer. That description did not excuse the seal confusion. It made the problem sound like someone whose work could be checked, rather than a villain waiting for a cultivated stranger to uncover him.

archive_08_006.speaker: he_xi
archive_08_006.text: If you go back wearing the archive's authority before anyone has given it to you, he will become certain the sword is the whole argument. He has already told people that officials prefer expensive paper. You can prove the copy's status tomorrow with someone appointed to do that. Today perhaps buy the bruised apple and let me finish bargaining for my mother's beans. I would enjoy a market morning that did not turn into testimony before I reached the last stall.

archive_08_007.speaker: narrator
archive_08_007.text: Yue bought the apple and ate around its bruise on the walk back. She wrote a brief factual report for the next day's duty list, naming the displayed source number, the shop mark and the unanswered acceptance question. The market woman's name was not necessary and remained unknown. Luo read the report on the fifty-seventh morning and wanted to call the copying a public service. Dai wanted to inspect the marks before using the phrase. Neither had seen the actual sheet. They appointed the ordinary reference clerk to compare a purchased example against its public source.

archive_08_008.speaker: narrator
archive_08_008.text: The clerk bought one sheet at the posted stall price and retained the transaction receipt. Its visible text matched an older common grazing provision, but the sheet omitted a later public amendment printed on the archive's current reference copy. The source number referred only to the older leaf. The round shop mark included the words reference supply in a ring too small for many readers to decipher. The clerk's report separated inaccurate currency, ambiguous presentation and the seller's unknown intent. Dai sent it to the market steward responsible for trading notices, who could require corrections through ordinary procedure.

archive_08_009.speaker: narrator
archive_08_009.text: The steward summoned the seller to an afternoon meeting at the lower receiving house. The invitation named the sheet and the specific problems, not a charge of stealing originals. He arrived carrying the whole stack and a box of stamped wrappers. He had copied from a reference sheet issued several years earlier, which remained a correct comparison of that older source. He had not asked whether a later amendment affected current use. The archive had no evidence that he had entered a closed room or taken a deposited object. Dai kept those invented accusations out of the meeting.

archive_08_010.speaker: narrator
archive_08_010.text: Luo showed the seller the later amendment and asked why he had used a round mark resembling the archive's seal. The man said buyers distrusted unstamped paper, and his shop had always used round stamps on calendars. Its design had become too close when he added a small book symbol. The market steward required clearer wording and a mark which did not suggest archive certification. The seller objected to paying for a new stamp until the steward pointed to the customers who had already paid for sheets unsuitable for the intended current application.

archive_08_011.speaker: narrator
archive_08_011.text: The seller would refund those misled about current official use or supply a corrected reference sheet at the buyer's choice, preserving receipt evidence under the steward's ordinary review. He could continue selling lawful clearly identified reference copies from the admitted public source, with the amendment included. The archive would publish a plain explanation of its own certification scope. Certification meant a checked comparison to named source fields on the issue date; it did not decide the applicant's present legal eligibility. A seller's misrepresentation and an office's different decision could otherwise become indistinguishable in a frustrated buyer's memory.

archive_08_012.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_08_012.text: I wanted the cheaper sheet to be an answer to the road and fee barriers I have been worrying about. It is an answer for someone who needs to read the wording at home. It is a worse answer for someone who thinks it carries the same attestation as our checked extract. We can help make useful reference copies available without pretending their price purchases every purpose. Put the amendment date on the front. Put the copy's status where a cold reader can see it before handing over a coin.

archive_08_013.speaker: narrator
archive_08_013.text: Dai surprised the seller by offering the current admitted public reference text without a proprietary copying charge. Standard consultation remained under the archive's published arrangement, and a commercial seller could reproduce this public wording subject to accurate attribution and no invented certification. The seller asked whether she would later change her mind if he made money. She said the access terms were written here, and his obligations were written beside them. The market steward witnessed the agreement. The conversation became less combative when each side could point to what the other actually required.

archive_08_014.speaker: narrator
archive_08_014.text: Yue prepared the plain explanation under paid assignment on the fifty-eighth day, with Dai checking the certification description and the market steward checking refund contacts. She added a question about old extracts: a correct old source comparison could remain old rather than become false. Readers should identify the issue date, named source and current office requirement. The cook read the draft and asked whether named source could be replaced by the book or paper copied. Dai accepted the simpler words with unexpected speed. She had learned that clarity could preserve an exact distinction more effectively than an admired technical phrase.

archive_08_015.speaker: narrator
archive_08_015.text: The market seller delivered corrected notices before the next local market. He had carved a rectangular shop mark because its corners looked less official to him. The text now stated reference copy, not certified extract, in large letters. He grumbled while posting the refund procedure, then admitted the new date line made it easier to know which stock to remove after an amendment. He brought the outdated stack to the steward for the promised account rather than quietly hiding it. His ordinary willingness to correct a profitable mistake would need follow-up, which the steward scheduled.

archive_08_016.speaker: narrator
archive_08_016.text: The woman who had asked about district acceptance came to the archive later that morning. She obtained the official requirement from the district office through the lower enquiry point and now knew which certified fields she needed. She qualified for the announced copying subsidy and accepted one standard sheet under its established declaration procedure. Luo gave her privacy to complete the short form. She told him the paper stall had been closer to her home. He said the corrected stall could still serve future reading needs. He did not demand she become grateful for the longer trip.

archive_08_017.speaker: narrator
archive_08_017.text: He delivered the corrected public notice to the school and two route stations under a paid local assignment. His father had begun the workshop's actual trial appointment, repairing small fitted pieces at a bench designed for his limited grip. The first day's work was poor enough to make the foreman shorten the task list, but not poor enough to end the trial. He wanted to hear every detail and feared sounding like a supervisor. His mother told him to ask about the day and let his father choose whether to describe the screws.

archive_08_018.speaker: narrator
archive_08_018.text: The market episode sharpened the vault discussion. A reference copy could be accurate and still unsuitable for one use; an original could be protected and still harder for a reader to reach. The board selected six public instruments for proposed transfer only after checked local references and the challenged-original travel procedure were agreed. The house instrument stayed locally accessible under the registrar's current advice. Private owners' distinct replies stayed outside the six-item list. The regional office confirmed funding for one necessary original-comparison journey per named active case, subject to its ordinary appointment rules.

archive_08_019.speaker: narrator
archive_08_019.text: Transport still depended on a safe ridge route. Tan packed the six selected public instruments into one loaned case under their assessed supports, leaving the second available for a different authorised need. Dai sealed the case after the counts and condition sheets were checked. The packed case stayed on the inspected dry shelf; it was not treated as delivered because the regional office had reserved space. Luo posted the local reference availability dates and the external original-request contact. A future move would alter where originals rested, not erase their movement history.

archive_08_020.speaker: narrator
archive_08_020.text: The first prolonged thaw began on the fifty-eighth afternoon. Ice loosened from the gutter and water moved steadily through the surface channel. The track steward's crew arrived on the fifty-ninth with the district surveyor's safe excavation plan. They would open the buried hatch from the stable side of the widened road, staying clear of the ravine edge. Tan showed them the current damp mark at the pantry wall. It had risen slightly. The crew leader recorded the change before anyone began digging, giving later observations an actual starting point.

archive_08_021.speaker: narrator
archive_08_021.text: Yue watched only from the permitted safe path. The first layer was ordinary gravel. Beneath it, the workers found a slab placed over the hatch frame during the road widening. Removing the slab exposed the old access cover, which had rusted against its edge. The crew used the approved levering tools and a supported approach, not a hand in the gap. When the cover lifted, cold water welled into the shallow opening. The leader stopped work long enough to measure the level and decide where released water could go safely.

archive_08_022.speaker: narrator
archive_08_022.text: The covered culvert held stones and compressed roots beyond the hatch. Some debris could be removed through the opening, but a larger obstruction lay near the ravine outlet. The crew cleared the reachable material and water began flowing faster. Its level remained too high for the expected channel fall. The outlet would need a separate safe-access operation while the slope was thawing. The surveyor issued an interim restriction: keep the archive's uphill lower storage empty, inspect the wall twice daily and prepare authorised movement if seepage rose to the marked warning line.

archive_08_023.speaker: narrator
archive_08_023.text: Luo disliked another interim result after so much labour. The crew leader asked whether he preferred a worker to enter the flooded passage to produce a complete-looking report. Luo said no immediately, then apologised for making disappointment sound like an instruction. The cleared hatch improved access and removed real blockage. It did not make the buried outlet safe to reach. Dai filed the warning line and designated the observation shifts. Yue copied the crew contact and next assessment time on the shared queue, where the former unanswered school message had once been only an old grievance.

archive_08_024.speaker: narrator
archive_08_024.text: The damp line rose by another finger's width that evening. Tan inspected the safe high shelves and found them dry. The low public references already raised onto rated supports remained above the projected shallow seepage route. Several empty floor-level containers could be moved farther from the uphill wall, giving water a visible path rather than hiding it behind stacked objects. Yue and the duty worker moved only those sound empty containers under the cleared route. She was grateful for work whose urgency did not require inventing either authority or strength.

archive_08_025.speaker: narrator
archive_08_025.text: The sixty-first morning froze the exposed hatch rim again. The track crew secured its cover and marked the work area, leaving drainage observation active until the outlet could be reached. The surveyor did not declare the partial clearance a cure. Snow returned above the ridge, and the regional transfer cart remained below. The packed public case rested where its seals and support could be checked. Dai counted the relevant private replies once more, remembering how quickly a room full of dry papers could make a danger feel less likely than its measurements said.

archive_08_026.speaker: narrator
archive_08_026.text: Earlier, at the fifty-ninth morning's follow-up, the seller returned to the market steward with four refund receipts and a fifth buyer he could not find. The steward recorded the uncompleted refund rather than letting four corrections make the fifth disappear. The seller seemed genuinely distressed now that the buyer had become a person he remembered instead of a missed sale. She had bought the sheet before dawn, carrying a basket with one broken handle. He could not supply her name. The steward authorised a notice at the route station where he had seen her leave.

archive_08_027.speaker: narrator
archive_08_027.text: Yue helped prepare that public notice during her paid copying assignment. It named the affected sheet and purchase period, offered the refund contact and included no claim that all copies were useless. The seller brought his old stamp to show the steward, then asked whether he could keep it for calendars after removing the book symbol. The steward wanted the revised impression checked first. The man agreed. Correcting a misleading mark did not require destroying every honest use its owner had made of it before he tried to look more official.

archive_08_028.speaker: narrator
archive_08_028.text: He told Yue the paper stall now displayed dates larger than prices, which had made one customer complain he could not see whether the bargain was cheap. She laughed and said clarity could evidently be overcorrected. The steward would have the seller adjust the layout at the follow-up. He looked pleased to carry a joke instead of another anxious household message. His father had completed three workshop trial days without losing the small screws. The foreman said this counted as improvement. His mother said it counted as a reason to wash hands before touching supper.

archive_08_029.speaker: narrator
archive_08_029.text: At the repaired school, the teacher used the paper-stall episode to ask pupils what made a written claim trustworthy. Several answered a red seal. One answered the writer being rich. The child who had proposed the fox selling invitations answered whether the question had actually been answered. The teacher sent their replies to Luo under the public lesson exchange. He spent longest looking at the rich answer, wondering how often the archive's own solemn furniture supplied that impression. Dai said their next notice should survive being pinned to a plain wall.

archive_08_030.speaker: narrator
archive_08_030.text: They tried it on the pantry's bare outer door. Staff walking past could find the issue date, source description and certification explanation without recognising an archive symbol. The cook complained that the paper obscured her reminder about clean scoops. Luo moved it to the adjacent plain board. A clear statement did not acquire priority over every other clear statement merely because it concerned official paper. Yue found the exercise unexpectedly cheering. The institution's dignity endured several domestic interruptions, and the notices became easier to use after each one.

archive_08_031.speaker: narrator
archive_08_031.text: The corrected grazing source drew an additional enquiry from a herder whose old allowance had been issued before the amendment. He did not assume the stall mistake cancelled his existing right. His district adviser would compare the original allowance date with the amendment's effect. The archive supplied the named historical source fields and left the legal decision to that process. Yue liked seeing a person use an old document intelligently rather than treat age as either automatic authority or automatic error. The sheet's past remained a fact to work with.

archive_08_032.speaker: narrator
archive_08_032.text: In the winter hall, the packed regional case tempted Luo to consider the transfer accomplished. Its neat supports, sealed lid and destination label made a future event look complete. Dai asked him to check the outward-receipt column. It was blank. He looked irritated, then wrote pending safe transport on the visible case tag. The lesson belonged to him because he had once moved a house instrument quickly and forgotten its return chain. Yue helped set the case behind the accessible inspection space, where its condition could still be checked without breaking the seal.

archive_08_033.speaker: narrator
archive_08_033.text: The six public instruments included the original school maintenance endowment. Its checked local references were ready for ordinary consultation, and the school trustee had accepted the board's authorised move subject to the regional retrieval terms. The later slate gift remained separately described, preventing the corrected funds from merging again simply because two original papers shared a crate. The catalogue kept their individual numbers and wrappers. One transport case could hold several documents without making them one agreement. Tan's spacing supports made the physical distinction as plain as Dai's movement list.

archive_08_034.speaker: narrator
archive_08_034.text: A member of the board disliked the cost of original-comparison travel support. He argued that most readers never challenged a copy. Luo agreed about the frequency and disagreed about the consequence. The one reader who needed physical endorsements could face an entire livelihood dispute. The regional office's funded journey rule for named active cases addressed a rare expensive need rather than subsidising every casual visit. The member asked for an annual review instead of removing the support. The board accepted review, leaving the current promise usable rather than indefinitely proposed.

archive_08_035.speaker: narrator
archive_08_035.text: Yue wrote to her mother on the fifty-eighth evening. She described a repaired roof, a paid winter appointment and a cook whose authority exceeded all the archive's seals at supper. She did not include the claimants' private histories. Her own staying was enough news for one page. The letter named the expected end of her term and the possibility that weather could delay departure. She asked about home without promising a spring arrival date she could not yet know. She left it for the next safe ridge relay, keeping its outward receipt among her personal letters. Delivery remained unconfirmed.

archive_08_036.speaker: narrator
archive_08_036.text: She nearly added a sentence saying she had become useful. The phrase looked unbearably eager once written. She crossed it out and described the stove debt correction instead, leaving its recipients unnamed. A concrete task might tell her mother what the weeks had been like without asking the reply to approve the person doing it. After sealing the letter, she sat with the discarded draft for a moment. Five trained stages had not removed the old wish to come home carrying a reason no one could dismiss.

archive_08_037.speaker: narrator
archive_08_037.text: That night she dreamed the archive shelves rose like trees while water climbed between them. In the dream she could lift every book with one hand and hold the whole building dry above the valley. Nobody needed to wait for a board or a crew. She woke angry at the pleasantness of the dream. Her hands felt heavy, her mouth tasted of sleep and the real wall remained beyond the bed curtain. She did not turn the dream into a new cultivation claim. It was a desire with an impossible body, familiar enough to hurt.

archive_08_038.speaker: narrator
archive_08_038.text: At breakfast Tan noticed her tired face and offered to swap a precise copying hour for straightforward label checking within the day's assignment. Yue accepted after Dai confirmed the priorities. The labels still required care, but no fragile original depended on her first attempt to recover concentration. The accommodation annoyed her because it was sensible. Tan did not pretend she should enjoy needing it. She gave her the list and asked for a report before lunch. Yue completed it well enough that the annoyance gradually lost its argument.

archive_08_039.speaker: narrator
archive_08_039.text: The preserved class book returned to its safe support after the lesson extracts were finished. Sun sent a new verse through her neighbour, clearly marked as a present composition rather than another recovered childhood page. She permitted the teacher to use it in the school lesson and the archive to keep a public reference copy. It concerned a fish who bought rain from a seller standing beside the pond. The paper smelled faintly of the neighbour's flour bag. Yue took the original offer to Dai, who catalogued its actual current date without making age a condition of merit.

archive_08_040.speaker: narrator
archive_08_040.text: The fish in Sun's verse promised the seller a pearl for seven days of rain. On the first day the sky remained blue, and the seller said a finer pearl would encourage the clouds. On the second day a passing heron ate the pearl before either could decide who owned it. On the third day rain fell on the pond, the seller's hat and a miser's washing line equally. The fish asked which part he had bought. The seller pointed to the drops that tasted best.

archive_08_041.speaker: narrator
archive_08_041.text: The fish tried to collect those drops in a shell, but they became pond water before he could count them. The seller offered an expensive lid. The fish declined and invited him to stand under a reed instead. By evening they were both wet, the washing line had collapsed and the heron had flown away with a sore throat from laughing. Sun's final line said that ordinary rain owed nobody a receipt. The teacher thought pupils would understand the fish sooner than the sentence about ownership.

archive_08_042.speaker: narrator
archive_08_042.text: Luo read the verse twice before saying he wanted its last line over his desk. Dai asked whether he intended to use a fish story to excuse missing receipts. He put the sheet down quickly enough to make Yue laugh. Sun's fable did not change the archive's accounts or the legal authority of a deed. It gave a room full of people worrying about records a way to laugh at the wish that the world would always answer in the form they preferred. The ordinary rain outside remained stubbornly literal.

archive_08_043.speaker: narrator
archive_08_043.text: The teacher replied that the fish needed a second pearl, otherwise the heron had acquired the best meal too cheaply. Sun answered through the permitted lesson channel that the heron had paid with a sore throat and no invitation to the fish's next dinner. A pupil added a snail carrying the seller's rejected lid uphill, hoping to sell it to someone else. Sun approved the addition as the pupil's own continuation. The archive kept the versions distinct rather than silently incorporating the snail into her original current verse.

archive_08_044.speaker: narrator
archive_08_044.text: He read the public lesson copy and asked why all wise animals seemed terrible at transport. The fish stayed in a pond, the heron stole freight and the snail carried a lid no customer had ordered. Luo said the archive had finally found its proper mythological staff. He declared himself the snail and Dai the fish. Dai refused a role assigned without consultation. The cook said she was plainly the heron and would like the pearl paid in apples. The joke lasted through the next meal, becoming less accurate and more useful each time someone repeated it.

archive_08_045.speaker: narrator
archive_08_045.text: The small fable also helped a boy ask a serious question. He wanted to know whether his family's roof complaint was merely ordinary rain for which nobody owed them an answer. The teacher brought that public question to the archive without exposing the household's private accounts. Dai explained that rain might owe no receipt, but a contractor promising a roof repair owed the work described in its agreement. A story's wisdom did not replace an actual promise. The boy received the plain public complaint contact, and the fable kept its proper size.

archive_08_046.speaker: narrator
archive_08_046.text: Yue liked the exchange enough to record the explanation in the lesson reply with Dai's approval. It prevented a pleasant metaphor from becoming an excuse for someone failing another person's roof. The teacher used the question to show pupils how stories and accounts asked different things. Sun was pleased, then irritated that everyone seemed surprised she had written something practical. She sent the archive a note telling it she had paid contractors herself. Luo read the note and decided the original fish would be safer above the cook's table than above his.

archive_08_047.speaker: narrator
archive_08_047.text: Outside, the track crew's thaw work drew local watchers. The district leader marked a safe viewing point far enough from the opening that children could see without crowding the tools. He did not invite them to help because their interest was lively. He Xi, passing on a paid local route, stopped to carry the crew's ordinary message to the steward. He had a current assignment authorising that additional delivery within the route rate. The hatch inspection belonged to trained workers and the district's maintenance funds, not to whichever neighbour happened to arrive with strong arms.

archive_08_048.speaker: narrator
archive_08_048.text: The steward showed up before the second day ended. He saw the compressed roots and stones for himself and accepted that the covered outlet required further work. His office would fund the safe-access operation when weather allowed it. He apologised to the school caretaker for the earlier unanswered flood report, naming the omitted inspection rather than calling the entire winter unavoidable. The caretaker wanted a future contact who would answer. The steward gave one and assigned the report a live work number. The apology acquired a practical handle someone could use later.

archive_08_049.speaker: narrator
archive_08_049.text: Tan walked the inside warning route with the night duty worker. They checked the damp mark, the cleared low floor and the path to the side door. The night worker pointed out that a lamp placed at one turn hid the floor's reflection beneath its glare. They moved it to a higher safe bracket and repeated the observation. Yue watched the change from the permitted dry side and saw the wall's lower line more clearly. It was the kind of improvement a daytime plan could miss unless the person working at night had room to object.

archive_08_050.speaker: narrator
archive_08_050.text: Dai asked the ordinary clinician how they should accommodate travellers who arrived wet during a prolonged storm. The advice concerned warm shelter, assessed injuries, dry clothes and referral needs, with symptoms reported rather than guessed at. The archive's two temporary beds remained the available places. If more people arrived, the board would need to arrange additional safe shelter with the village rather than stack bodies against the hall exit. Luo contacted the receiving-house steward while the relay worked. Preparation widened the possible response without making the mountain kitchen unlimited.

archive_08_051.speaker: narrator
archive_08_051.text: Yue folded dry traveller blankets with the store assistant during her paid movement assignment. They found one blanket whose middle seam had opened. The cook could repair it after her shift if she chose a separately paid mending task under the ordinary household-supply account. She accepted the small task and demanded good thread rather than vague gratitude. Yue fetched the thread from its authorised store drawer. The blanket would be ready before the storm evening. A future guest would feel warmth without knowing how many small agreements had kept its seam together.

archive_08_052.speaker: narrator
archive_08_052.text: The still-sick clerk woke long enough to ask whether the drainage queue had been checked. Luo told him the substitute had sent the report and received the reply. The clerk asked a second time, unable to believe the work had proceeded without his own reminder. Dai brought him the completed action number, then took it away when he tried to begin another task from bed. His usefulness had become a habit that illness could not simply switch off. The new system needed to protect him from his devotion as well as cover his absence.

archive_08_053.speaker: narrator
archive_08_053.text: Tan admitted she sometimes envied the clerk's devotion because it made other people trust him immediately. She wanted to be trusted for saying wait, do less or stop. Those instructions sounded less generous, especially when a person had come far for a paper. Yue said the night lamp's new position had looked generous to the duty worker, though nobody had called it that. Tan thought for a while and said perhaps she should stop accepting the easiest vocabulary for her own job. They carried the last dry blankets to their proper shelf before supper.

archive_08_054.speaker: narrator
archive_08_054.text: The upper path watcher brought the storm forecast before the two stranded travellers appeared. Falling temperatures after the thaw would leave ice across the quarry route. Local walkers were warned at the village gate and route stations. The two travellers had started from farther north before the new warning reached them. The watcher found them at the safe junction and brought them down after assessing the open approach. Their arrival would not prove the warning effort useless. It would prove why warning and receiving arrangements had to exist together.

archive_08_055.speaker: narrator
archive_08_055.text: On the sixty-second afternoon, a storm drove two travellers from the upper quarry path toward the archive. A local road watcher brought them to the side entrance after checking the approach. They had been returning to a nearby settlement when falling ice blocked their path, and the watcher would not send them back into the same hazard. The two temporary receiving-room sleeping places were available. Dai admitted them under the existing traveller shelter arrangement while the clinician assessed a swollen ankle. Neither person had come to consult records. Their need was warmth and a safe place to wait.

archive_08_056.speaker: narrator
archive_08_056.text: The cook issued two additional daily shares conservatively for their evening admission, in addition to the resident ten. She used one and a half cooking bundles for the larger hot pot and bedding-water needs, recording the extra half. The travellers' private details stayed in the guest book; the common stock notice needed only their number and the actual consumption. Yue carried the approved extra bedding from the traveller cupboard. The preservation visitor had returned its earlier place, and the mattresses were dry. Practical preparation had left room for people nobody knew by name.

archive_08_057.speaker: narrator
archive_08_057.text: One traveller slept almost immediately after the clinical check. The other kept apologising for the second share because he had eaten at noon. The cook told him the share was her planning entry and his supper was becoming cold while he tried to correct it. He ate. Dai sat nearby to explain the next route assessment, and Luo found a public picture book which required little reading. Yue watched the man's shoulders lower as he looked at a drawing of summer boats. The room's hospitality did not need a testimony in return.

archive_08_058.speaker: narrator
archive_08_058.text: Yue saw their footprints in the courtyard slush and thought of the paper buyer's basket, the sick clerk's bed and her mother's unanswered letter. The archive held many forms of waiting, some named in a register and others too ordinary to file. She could respond to a present wet coat without settling every future claim. She helped the duty worker clear the entry mats and returned the broom to its hook. The picture book waited inside, its summer boats bright enough to give a stranger's eyes somewhere warm to rest.

archive_08_059.speaker: narrator
archive_08_059.text: As the kitchen enlarged its pot for the guests, Luo took the fish fable off the cook's table so it would not become splashed with soup. The cook told him to put it in the public reference tray rather than carry it to his desk and forget it there. He obeyed with a theatrical bow. Dai checked the storm duty page and asked for the wall's latest measurement. Tan gave the actual line, still below warning. Their laughter and the report occupied the same room. Neither made the other less necessary.

archive_08_060.speaker: narrator
archive_08_060.text: At the close of day sixty-two, seven more days had used seventy resident shares and two guest shares. The food balance fell from eight hundred and sixty-three to seven hundred and ninety-one. Two cold days, three mild half-use days and two further cold days burned five and a half charcoal sacks, leaving seventy-two and a half. Cooking wood used six ordinary bundles and the larger pot's one and a half, leaving ninety-three and a half. The figures did not decide when the travellers could go home. They told the board what welcoming them had actually used.

archive_08_061.speaker: narrator
archive_08_061.text: The duty worker brought a dry board to the winter hall and laid out the ordinary stop signals for the night team. Yue checked her assigned station and the route to it before the wind grew louder. Her four opened pairs would not make the wall dry. Her practiced feet and clear calls could keep someone from entering the wrong aisle. She tied her coat firmly, left the sword covered and listened for the first report from the uphill room.

archive_08_062.speaker: narrator
archive_08_062.text: The storm thickened after supper until the courtyard drain disappeared beneath slush. The track crew could not reach the outlet safely, the regional cart could not collect its case and the two guests could not return by the quarry path. Dai checked the uphill wall one last time with the duty worker. Its warning mark remained just above the damp line. Yue stood in the winter hall beside the picture book's summer boats and heard the gutter change from dripping to a heavy continuous rush. The archive's next night would require its prepared plans to become actions.
